subject: Recap: Burst-duration & hot-path sizing for ParcelCo
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@parcelco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-08-03T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: Burst-duration & hot-path sizing for ParcelCo

Hi Alice — thanks again for taking time today. Quick post-call recap and the asks we discussed so we can move to a pilot sizing: 

What we heard (please confirm):
- Primary product path is an interactive user chat (streaming enabled) used for order lookup and guided support.
- Typical request mix: 60% short lookups (~80 tokens), 30% mid-length assistance (~400 tokens), 10% long-form summarization (~2k tokens).
- Expected steady-state: ~18 QPS (~14k tokens/sec aggregate).
- Peak burst: estimated 1,200 simultaneous sessions in a ~3–7 minute window; heavy tails last up to 12 minutes during promotions.
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end (model) <= 350ms for streaming interactive flows; fallback model acceptable at higher latency but must keep p99 < 2s.

Immediate asks (deliverables you offered after the call):
1) Representative 1–2 hour request logs (CSV or JSON) showing timestamps, tokens_in, tokens_out, intent tag, and whether streaming was used.
2) Token distribution by intent or endpoint (per-request token counts).
3) Confirmation of peak-burst duration (is 3–7 minutes the right window? you mentioned sometimes up to 12).
4) Any contract constraints around PII/retention we should be aware of for the pilot.

What we'll do on our side:
- Quick sizing pass based on your logs to estimate tokens/sec, QPS, and concurrency mapping to instance types (dedicated vs hosted).
- Propose a pilot config (streaming slots, KV cache settings, batching window) and a recommended SLO cadence.
- If pilot looks good, propose a 4‑week pilot that covers a production-like promotional period.

Attachments: initial-ask-checklist.pdf (short checklist of the fields that are most useful).

Next steps: If you can drop the logs and token profile, Marissa and I will turn around a sizing proposal within 48 hours. Also confirm if we should include your security contact on the next exchange.

Thanks — Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Enterprise Sales 
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@parcelco.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, ParcelCo Eng <eng@parcelco.com>
Date: 2025-08-04T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Burst-duration & hot-path sizing for ParcelCo

Thanks Stephanie — great summary and yes, that captures the call. A few quick answers and I attached a small token profile CSV (parcelco_token_profile.csv) with anonymized samples. 

- Peak burst window: typically 4–9 minutes; during the last promotion we saw a 12-minute tail as I mentioned.
- The mix and token numbers in your note look right; we included intent labels in column `intent`.
- Security: we can share logs with PII redacted; our InfoSec mavens want retention not to exceed 30 days for the pilot. Will loop them in if needed.

Two quick questions: 
1) For streaming, if we enable chunked output, what is the expected model-side p95 delta vs non-streaming? 
2) If we see a tail beyond 12 minutes, does Redwood have autoscaling for burst prolongation or do we rely on pre-warmed capacity?

I'll upload the full 2 hour sample to the Drive folder by EOD.

—Alice
Alice Johnson
Head of Product Operations
ParcelCo
alice.johnson@parcelco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@parcelco.com>
Cc: ParcelCo Eng <eng@parcelco.com>
Date: 2025-08-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Burst-duration & hot-path sizing for ParcelCo

Hi all — I pulled the attached token profile and did a first-pass sizing note (attached: sizing-proposal-v1.pdf). High-level observations:

- Token distribution: median ~220 tokens/request, mean ~370 (skewed by long-form).
- Estimated tokens/sec at steady-state: ~14–16k t/s (matches the call). Peak observed instant t/s during the sample ~280k t/s for ~5 minutes.
- Mapping to QPS: assuming typical streaming chunk size ~128 tokens and average 350 tokens/request, peak instantaneous QPS equivalent ~800–1,000 concurrent streaming sessions.

Recommendations (pilot):
- Reserve 6–8 NVidia-A100 equivalent GPUs for pilot peak reservation with autoscale headroom to 12 for prolonged tails. This assumes continuous KV cache for repeated prefixes (order lookups) and a batching-friendly window of 20ms per shard.
- Streaming config: use chunk sizes of ~128 tokens and enable early flush for short intents to keep p95 model latency within ~300–350ms. Expect an additional ~30–50ms overhead per chunk vs non-streaming RPC.
- Fallback plan: provide a smaller quantized model variant for background jobs; hold the high‑quality variant for interactive sessions.

Open items:
1) Confirm whether your environment requires private deployment (VPC/on-prem) for the pilot — that impacts cold-starts and pre-warming.
2) Share 1–3 production days (not just 2 hours) if possible to validate sustained tails.
3) Legal/security retention cap — if 30 days is a hard cap that’s fine for a pilot, we’ll note it in the pilot plan.

I included an abbreviated SLO table in the PDF; Marissa (me) happy to walk through it.

Best —
Marissa Cole
Performance Solutions
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@parcelco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, ParcelCo Eng <eng@parcelco.com>
Date: 2025-08-06T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Burst-duration & hot-path sizing for ParcelCo — next steps

Thanks both — this is perfect. Quick answers and proposed next steps: 

1) Streaming latency delta: based on our benchmarks and Marissa's config, model-side p95 delta for chunked streaming vs non-streaming should be ~30–60ms depending on chunking policy; end-to-end p95 depends on network but we usually see <100ms platform overhead on hosted deployments. We'll surface exact numbers in the pilot proposal.

2) Autoscaling vs pre-warmed: Redwood Dedicated supports autoscale with a policy for prolonged tails (we can hold burst pre-warm credit and then scale programmatically). For the pilot I recommend: reserve pre-warmed capacity to cover 70% of expected peak, and allow autoscale-to-cap at 150% for unexpected tails — this gives a balance of cost predictability and resilience.

Proposed timeline:
- Today/TOM: ParcelCo uploads 2h sample + redaction confirmation (Alice).
- +48 hours: Redwood sizing proposal and SLO table (Marissa & I).
- +5 business days: mutually agreed pilot config and contract addendum (if security/retention OK).
- Pilot duration: 4 weeks including one promotional peak window.

Action items for ParcelCo: please upload the logs to the Drive link and drop a short note if 30-day retention is acceptable for the pilot (or if InfoSec needs to be looped in). Also confirm whether you want the pilot on Redwood Hosted (fastest path) or Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPUs).

I’m copying the Drive and HubSpot links here: https://hubspot.company/contacts/PC-2025-0912 and https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1ParcelCoPilot. Also attached: sizing-proposal-v1.pdf (initial recommendation).

If you’re good with the timeline, I’ll open a DocuSign for the pilot addendum and we’ll schedule a quick 30-min kickoff for next week.

Best —
Stephanie
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
